compatibility.title: Which Kia and Hyundai Models Use the G4NA?
compatibility.intro: The G4NA is the 2.0‑litre naturally aspirated member of Hyundai‑Kia's Nu family of petrol engines. It was fitted primarily to mid‑size saloons, SUVs and MPVs from 2010 to 2018, replacing the older Theta II G4KD in many applications.

failures.title: Kia G4NA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Coil pack and ignition system failure
items.whatHappens: Like many Hyundai‑Kia petrol engines of this era, the G4NA is prone to coil pack failure. Symptoms include engine misfire, rough idle, loss of power, and the check engine light illuminating. This is the single most common issue reported on the G4NA.
items.repairVsReplace: Coil packs are relatively inexpensive (around £50-£150 each) and straightforward to replace. This is a routine maintenance item, not a reason for engine replacement. Read our full ignition system failure guide

items.title: O2 sensor failure
items.whatHappens: Oxygen sensors can fail over time, leading to poor fuel economy, check engine light, and in some cases, MOT failure due to emissions issues.
items.repairVsReplace: O2 sensors are replaceable (around £100-£250 each) and this is standard maintenance on higher‑mileage petrol engines.

items.title: Oil consumption
items.whatHappens: Some G4NA engines can develop oil consumption as they age, typically due to piston ring wear or valve stem seal wear. This is more common on higher‑mileage examples.
items.repairVsReplace: If oil consumption is moderate (up to 1 litre per 1,000 miles), regular top‑ups are the standard approach. If consumption becomes excessive, piston rings or valve stem seals may need replacement - this typically requires a rebuild.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the G4NA
variants.intro: The G4NA is a specific engine code within the Hyundai‑Kia Nu family of petrol engines. Unlike some families that fragment into many sub‑codes with different hardware, the G4NA's variants are primarily distinguished by fuel delivery system and power output. Nu Family Overview: The Nu family includes: - G4NA - 2.0L MPI / GDi, 150-162 hp, 2.0‑litre naturally aspirated petrol - G4NB - 2.0L MPI, lower‑output variant fitted to some markets - G4NC - 2.0L Smartstream successor, fitted to later models - G4FD - 1.6L GDi, fitted to i30 and Cee'd Within the G4NA, the key distinctions are: - MPI (Multi‑Point Injection) variant - 150 hp (110 kW), fitted to entry‑level models; uses traditional port fuel injection - GDi (Gasoline Direct Injection) variant - 162 hp (119 kW), fitted to higher‑spec models; uses direct injection; more prone to carbon buildup on intake valves - Market‑specific tuning - Some markets received different calibration for emissions compliance How to confirm your code: 1. On the engine - the G4NA code is stamped on the engine block. Look for "G4NA" on the identification plate on the front or side of the engine. 2. On the V5C logbook - the engine number is listed; cross‑reference with Hyundai‑Kia parts systems. 3. VIN decode - use a Hyundai‑Kia VIN decoder; the engine type will be shown. 4. Registration lookup - enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact fitment. Similar‑looking codes it is commonly confused with: - Kia G4KD - the Theta II 2.0 MPI predecessor, fitted to earlier Sportage and Optima models; similar displacement but different engine family - Kia G4LC - the 1.4‑litre Kappa petrol engine, fitted to smaller models; completely different architecture - Kia G4FP - the Smartstream 1.6 T‑GDi successor, fitted to newer models; turbocharged and significantly different

relatives.description: G4KD (Theta II 2.0 MPI): - the 2.0-litre Theta II petrol that preceded the G4NA in earlier Sportage, Optima and i40 models. The G4NA (Nu) brought improved fuel economy, reduced emissions and better low-end torque.

G4NC / G4FP (Smartstream 2.0): - the Smartstream 1.6 T-GDi and 2.0 MPI successors, fitted to newer Sportage, Optima and i40 models from 2018 onwards. They feature improved fuel injection and emissions systems.

variants.closing: Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The G4NA MPI and GDi versions have different fuel systems, injectors, and engine management. A GDi engine fitted to an MPI‑spec vehicle will require different fuel delivery components and ECU programming. The Smartstream G4FP (turbo) is not a direct swap at all.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement G4NA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used G4NA makes sense for lower‑value Optima, Sportage or i40 examples where the car itself is worth under £3,000-£4,000. The key requirement is documented service history with the correct oil specification, and evidence that the coil packs and O2 sensors have been addressed if over 80,000 miles. The primary risk with used units is undisclosed ignition issues - insist on a diagnostic check and compression test before purchase. Used units typically cost £350-£800. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper G4NA recon includes new coil packs, new spark plugs, new O2 sensors, full gasket set, and inspection of the piston rings and valve stem seals for oil consumption. This is the right call for most replacements - you get a like‑new unit with the known weak points already addressed, backed by 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned units typically cost £1,000-£2,000. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for higher‑value examples or where the existing engine has suffered bottom‑end failure or excessive oil consumption requiring new pistons and rings. An upgraded rebuild should include new piston rings, bearings, oil pump, and a full set of gaskets. For standard applications, reconditioned is usually more cost‑effective. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Kia and Hyundai specialists - nationwide coverage with 12‑month warranty on labour and parts. View supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The G4NA sits in mid‑range Kia and Hyundai models - Kia Optima (£3,000-£10,000), Kia Sportage (£4,000-£14,000), Hyundai i40 (£2,500-£9,000). A £1,000-£2,000 reconditioned engine plus £500-£800 fitting is a significant investment - typically 20-40% of the vehicle's value. For lower‑value examples, a used engine with documented maintenance history may be more economic. For well‑maintained, high‑spec examples, the investment is usually justified. The G4NA's simplicity and parts availability make it a viable candidate for repair rather than scrapping in most cases.

items.question: What are the common problems with the Kia G4NA engine?
items.answer: The G4NA's most common issues are coil pack failure (misfire, rough idle, loss of power), O2 sensor failure (check engine light, emissions issues), and oil consumption at higher mileages. The engine is generally reliable when properly maintained. Coil pack failure is the most common issue. O2 sensor replacement is standard maintenance. Regular oil changes are essential for longevity.

items.question: Is the G4NA a reliable engine?
items.answer: Yes - the G4NA is generally considered a reliable and durable engine. With regular maintenance (oil changes using the correct specification, coil packs replaced at 80,000+ miles), G4NA engines regularly exceed 150,000 miles. The MPI version is considered more reliable than the GDi version due to the GDi's carbon buildup on intake valves. MPI version is simpler and more reliable. GDi version offers more power but needs carbon cleaning. Regular maintenance is the key to longevity.
